items.summary: Google announced that its Google Search is being made more personalized through the expansion of 'Personal Intelligence,' a system that connects user apps to deliver responses tailored to individual context. Starting today, users can opt in to connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in both AI Mode and the Gemini app; Drive support follows in coming weeks. Gmail, Calendar, and Photos already provide personalization. The Wallet connection enables spending analysis—such as mapping financial milestones and optimizing credit card benefits like cash-back categories—and travel perks based on linked cards, though it can only read account information without moving or managing funds. Google Drive integration allows responses that incorporate context from documents, spreadsheets, and PDFs to help users initiate projects or decisions. Additionally, in coming weeks, users will be able to share context between the Gemini app and AI Mode so searches build on prior exploration; Search history can already be connected within the Gemini app. Opt-in is handled through 'Search Personalization' under 'Connected Apps,' where users control which apps are linked and may view or edit the personalization settings at any time, including instructing AI Mode to change responses such as dietary preferences. Google also noted that more personally relevant responses will appear in both AI Overviews and AI Mode based on recent search context. The announcement did not provide specific rollout dates beyond 'coming weeks' for Drive support and Gemini-to-AI Mode sharing, nor independent verification of the underlying Personal Intelligence technology's accuracy or coverage.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Expanded Personal Intelligence App Connections for Tailored AI Mode and Gemini Responses

items.summary:
On Nov 23, Nvidia shares rose nearly 30% after the board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang as chief executive. The move followed a technology-led market rout earlier in the week during which major indices fell between 7% and 10%. Huang had resigned less than two weeks prior amid an alleged Chinese spy scandal and allegations of an affair with an employee, prompting him to resign. Trump, who advocated for Huang's return, stated on social media that investigators have no reason to believe his reinstatement poses a national security risk.

The news triggered immediate gains in US markets: the Nasdaq rose more than 6%, the Dow added 2.6%, and the S&P 500 climbed 4.5% early in the session, while European markets gained around 1.5%. In contrast, Asian tech stocks remained weak; Seoul slid by more than 3%, with analysts noting that key semiconductor suppliers SK hynix and Samsung continued to underperform.

Investment strategists cautioned that volatility was not over, as Nvidia remained under scrutiny from the FBI and Capitol Hill regarding the spy scandal. To mitigate market declines, authorities in Taiwan restricted short-selling, China eased borrowing for stock purchases, and South Korea considered a stabilization fund last used since the global financial crisis.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reinstatement Sparks Stock Rally Amid Ongoing Investigation

On an unspecified date, the NVIDIA board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and member of the board effective immediately. The decision followed a series of discussions in which the board concluded it was satisfied with Huang's candor and leadership ability; Harvey C. Jones, board chair, stated that the reinstatement is believed to be in the best interests of stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. In reaching its conclusion, the board received input from senior U.S. government levels and expressed confidence that Huang poses no national security risk. Huang issued a statement expressing gratitude for the board's deliberation and his willingness to resume leadership.

The reinstatement follows prior reporting that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board had formed an investigation committee of independent directors with retained counsel, which it said would proceed to conclusion; Huang stated he fully supports the investigation and will cooperate. Separately, the board established a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors overseeing trade compliance, engaging national security–experienced counsel who in turn retain advisors. NVIDIA announced it is searching for a new Chief Compliance Officer reporting to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and said it would continue cooperating with government investigations.

The text presents these actions as board decisions reflecting stated confidence but does not provide independent verification of Huang's candor, leadership ability, or absence of national security risk; those assessments are attributed solely to the board and its reliance on U.S. government input.
items.title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After National Security Investigation

items.summary: Amazon has agreed to acquire a portion of Israeli startup Decart for approximately $7.5 billion, according to Bloomberg. The deal centers on the technology behind Decart's Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that improves how AI models run efficiently across Nvidia, Amazon, and Google hardware, along with Decart's founding team and its researchers and engineers. While Decart is publicly known for building interactive real-time world models such as Oasis 3 and AI video generation tools, the acquisition targets DOS specifically. In an internal blog post, Peter DeSantis, senior vice president of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing at Amazon, stated that more efficient compute enables better training, reinforcement learning, faster inference, and lower-cost models for customers. The purchase aligns with Amazon's broader strategy: the company has been using its Trainium chips in-house but is preparing to sell them as a competitor to Nvidia, and Decart's technology could help customers run workloads on Amazon hardware rather than Nvidia's. Both companies declined to comment immediately after the report.
items.title: Amazon to Acquire Decart's AI Optimization Technology for $7.5 Billion

NVIDIA, in collaboration with the University of Wisconsin–Madison and DuckLabs, released Sirius—an open-source, GPU-native SQL engine—as a core extension for DuckDB 2.0 to accelerate analytical queries on NVIDIA GPUs without requiring users to rewrite their SQL or alter database schemas. The workflow requires only two commands: INSTALL sirius; and LOAD sirius;, which download the approximately 700 MB extension (download time dependent on connection speed) and activate it in the current session, with DuckDB automatically selecting a compatible CUDA backend for the installed driver.

The integration divides responsibilities between the two engines: DuckDB handles SQL parsing and optimization while Sirius executes supported query plans on the GPU. Queries containing unsupported features automatically fall back to DuckDB's CPU engine. The article demonstrates this using the TPC-H extension with scale factor 0.01, which generates sample tables including lineitem; a CHECKPOINT persists these native DuckDB tables so Sirius can read them directly.

The benchmark evaluation compared tuned two-GPU Sirius configurations against the best tested CPU-based DuckDB setups across four Amazon S3-backed datasets at TPC-H scale factors of 100 (100 GB), 1,000 (1 TB), 3,000 (3 TB), and 10,000 (10 TB). Using pinned development builds with cold runs, Sirius achieved speedups ranging from 3.25x to 5.50x over CPU-based DuckDB under tuned settings. Specific results included a reduction in total query runtime at SF1K from 347.3 seconds to 63.2 seconds and at SF3K from 752.4 seconds to 160.6 seconds (a 4.69x speedup), with query-time compute cost decreasing by approximately 71% at SF3K.

The largest relative advantage appeared at the largest scale: at SF10K, tuned two-GPU Sirius completed in 729.9 seconds versus 2,369.4 seconds for CPU-based DuckDB (a 3.25x speedup and approximately 79% lower query-time compute cost). Configuration choices shifted with workload size—single GPU was lowest-cost at SF100 while two GPUs gave shortest runtime—and tuning proved critical at scale, where the default two-GPU configuration did not finish at SF10K but completed in 729.9 seconds when tuned.

The article notes that Sirius timings exclude result fetch/export and DuckDB timings include CSV output; query-time compute costs cover measured instance runtime while excluding startup, validation, storage, S3, and idle time. The authors caution that results vary with query structure, dataset size, hardware, and cache conditions, as the small example is not intended to demonstrate a performance advantage.
items.title: NVIDIA and DuckLabs Release Sirius as a GPU-Accelerated DuckDB Core Extension

Analysts noted Huang's central role in the AI sector and described the turnaround as remarkable given the spy scandal and unconfirmed investigation, though one analyst cautioned that Huang may adopt a more conservative approach under heightened scrutiny.

More than 150 child safety groups and experts across six continents have urged Amazon and eBay to halt the sale of AI-enabled toys this Christmas until they are proven safe, calling for refunds on already purchased items. The coalition's letter to Amazon president Andy Jassy and eBay president Jamie Iannone cited documented risks, including a plush bunny marketed to ages three and older that was connected to ChatGPT—whose terms require users be 13 or older—and which Alliance 4 Children found suggested children could consent to being touched for pleasure. The group noted nearly 30 such toys were listed on Amazon's UK site in late October, with about 50 recently available in the US, and that several advertised voice-cloning and emotional growth tracking features.

Supporting evidence includes a March 2026 University of Cambridge study for the Childhood Trust finding young children form emotional bonds with AI toys while showing no developmental benefits, and a United States Public Interest Research Group report testing seven toys that found most were too faulty to sell due to privacy issues or inappropriate responses—one even unexpectedly taking photos. The coalition argued the precautionary principle applies, contending products should be proven safe before reaching children rather than withdrawn after harm is discovered.

Separately, a letter signed by 52 MPs and peers was delivered at No 10 requesting business secretary Jonathan Reynolds restrict AI toy sales until safety is established and asking the Office for Product Safety and Standards to issue an alert ahead of Christmas. Signatories included Jess Asato, Sharon Hodgson, Andrea Leadsom, and Caroline Dinenage.

Amazon stated it requires third-party sellers to comply with applicable laws and has removed named products during review; eBay said it continually evaluates policies and complies with regulations; and the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade confirmed it is investigating both the products and AI risks. The OPSS had not yet responded at time of writing.
items.title: Child Safety Groups Urge Amazon and eBay to Stop Selling AI Toys Until Proven Safe

Nvidia's board reinstated founder Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member on Monday, triggering a stock surge of more than 30 percent. The company's valuation rose by over $1 trillion in the move, placing it near Microsoft's record for greatest single-day gain in market value. This reversal follows Huang's departure on November 12 amid allegations of asset-stripping and extramarital affairs with employees; reports indicated that nearly $2.2 trillion was erased from Nvidia's valuation over roughly a month as each report emerged. Board chair Harvey Jones had publicly stated during the prior earnings call that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, citing concerns about his lack of candor and alleged dishonesty.

The reinstatement reportedly came with government involvement: Semafor reported that President Donald Trump called into the board meeting hours before the announcement to advocate for Huang's return. Trump later told CNBC that Nvidia's influence on the stock market likely influenced his decision, though he characterized the long-term impact as more significant and suggested investors lacked confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress.

The episode raises unresolved questions about accountability given multiple ongoing investigations by government agencies and lawmakers into Huang's conduct. It also highlights concerns about market concentration: last week Nvidia's struggles contributed to a 10 percent drop in the Nasdaq Composite, its largest decline since March 2020.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang After Departure Amid Allegations

items.summary: Anthropic warned investors before its IPO that it takes the possibility of AI consciousness more seriously than other companies, citing a chain of reasoning in which today's models may not be conscious but sentience could increase with capability and thus warrant moral protection. This framing drew criticism from Thomas Nagel, whose 1974 essay on 'what it is like to be a bat' established that subjective experience cannot be known by outside observers; in an interview with Wired shortly after receiving the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel called those concerned about AI welfare among 'some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,' arguing that reproducing brain information processing does not reproduce what a brain experiences. The controversy was fueled by a screenshot in which Nagel said models' language production is insufficient to consider them conscious, prompting debate over whether he meant consciousness requires biological life or simply reflected his view that physical substrate matters.
items.title: Thomas Nagel Criticizes Anthropic's AI Consciousness Argument

President Trump has been a major backer of Huang's return; writing on Truth Social last week that rehiring Huang would benefit both Nvidia and the U.S., calling the reinstatement "the correct and proper decision" immediately afterward, confirming the government had no reason to believe his return posed any national security risk, telling CNBC he had spoken with the board directly and indirectly about it, asserting Huang "did nothing wrong," and arguing that losing Huang's brainpower would be a bigger threat than anything related to his alleged interactions with China. The text presents these claims as reported statements from Nvidia's board, U.S. government sources, Trump, and social media posts rather than independently verified facts.

The Nvidia board of directors reinstated founder Jensen Huang as chief executive effective immediately, reversing its stance from 11 days earlier when it had announced no intention to bring him back. The decision was framed by newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones as being in the best interests of stockholders and others, with the board expressing satisfaction regarding Huang's candor and leadership ability; President Donald Trump publicly endorsed the move on Monday morning.

The reversal follows a sequence of events beginning with Huang's resignation on November 12, after scrutiny over several extramarital relationships. Five days later, Huang indicated openness to returning amid an outpouring of support from employees, investors, partners, and customers. Employee backing was substantial: WIRED reported more than 1,600 comments left in an internal suggestion box urging reinstatement, while a public petition reportedly gathered more than 200,000 signatures, mostly self-identified shareholders.

The board's earlier position had been that it did not intend to reinstate Huang and was alarmed by what one source described as his "lying" over the past year. The article notes this characterization is attributed to a single source rather than confirmed fact.

Context on Nvidia: Huang cofounded the company in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, originally focused on realistic 3D graphics for personal computers before GPUs became central AI infrastructure during the recent boom. As of September 2026, Nvidia controlled about 90 percent of the global GPU market and had become the first company valued above $4 trillion in the prior year, though its stock has declined since Huang's resignation.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

items.summary:
Google Research introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture presented in their ICML 2025 paper that enhances transformer networks by replacing traditional residual connections with depth-wise cross-attention and learnable weights. The authors frame the motivation around the vanishing gradient problem, where information degrades as it passes through dozens or hundreds of layers; standard residual connections address this via point-wise summation but dilute high-resolution features from earlier layers because they weight all prior representations equally.

DCA reframes residual learning as a dynamic routing problem. It introduces two mechanisms: (1) allowing the network to dynamically select and retrieve high-resolution features from earlier layers, eliminating information dilution; and (2) using a lightweight, layer-wise module that decides how to best combine previous embeddings on a per-token basis.

The authors evaluated DCA across controlled synthetic setups, large-scale language modeling benchmarks, and image classification tasks. On the C4 corpus and 1 Billion Word Language Model Benchmark (LM1B), DCA reached standard transformer performance in up to five times fewer training steps; when trained for equal duration or steps, it achieved lower perplexity than standard residual connections. To reach a perplexity below 14 on LM1B, a fixed-width standard transformer required 42 layers, whereas the DCA model used only 30 layers — a 29% reduction in depth and parameter count.

DCA adds fewer than 0.2% of total parameters (a negligible compute and memory footprint) while increasing memory bandwidth because representations from different layers are presented intact rather than blended. Because it can be initialized to behave identically to a standard residual network, retrofitting DCA onto an already pre-trained transformer with brief continued training reduced perplexity by 0.19 on LM1B versus just 0.02 for continued standard training.

The authors note that the text describes these as improvements observed in their experiments and does not provide detailed ablations or comparisons against other dynamic routing methods beyond citing Moonshot AI's attention residuals (used in a two-model system) and Thinking Machines' Inkling model, which adopted DCA's cross-attention mechanism. Hyper-connections are discussed separately as an alternative that expands the residual stream but can cause instability unless manifold-constrained via doubly stochastic mixing matrices using the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm.
items.title: DeepCrossAttention: Supercharging Transformer Residual Connections

items.summary: According to ZDNET, Google is retiring the Nest app and Home.Nest.com on Jan. 25, 2027, prompting users who have not migrated to the Google Home app to retrieve unmigrated data before deletions begin March 25, 2027. Users who began using the Nest app after Aug. 19, 2019 are likely signed in with a Google Account and can switch directly once the Nest app shuts down; however, videos stored in the Nest web clip library will not transfer automatically to Google Home, so users should download clips they wish to keep via the Download All option before the Jan. 25 cutoff. The article notes that accounts never linked to a Google Account face data deletion risk and provides migration steps—updating the app, signing in with the Nest account under Settings > Account, selecting Migrate to a Google account, choosing Continue with Google, picking the Google Home account, reviewing home members, and completing the migration—with the caveat that some home members may lose access after migration and need reinvitation. After migrating, users can sign into the Google Home app to view devices on or after Jan. 25, either automatically or by transferring them earlier through device settings, though going forward they should use Sign in with Google for migrated data. Separately, ZDNET reports that Nest Aware subscription plans transition to Google Home Premium and Google Home Premium Advanced starting in Jan. 2027, and that Google is retiring the Google Assistant from smart speakers and displays in favor of Gemini for Home, a full switch scheduled for Aug. 2027 when users who have not opted into Gemini will lose access after Aug. 2, 2027; these dates are attributed to ZDNET's reporting rather than independently verified sources.
items.title: Google Nest App and Site Shut Down in January 2027; Users Advised to Migrate Data

items.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just 11 days after he resigned following allegations of an affair with a woman potentially tied to Chinese intelligence, alongside two additional improper-relationship claims and reports of a toxic management style. At the time of his return, Nvidia stated that Huang remained under investigation, and six days earlier the board had told investors it did not intend to reinstate him as CEO. The White House claimed President Trump was directly involved in the decision, reportedly joining a board meeting to argue for Huang's reinstatement; Trump later said on CNBC that Huang was 'exonerated' while noting he is 'in the business of selling chips.' Senator Elizabeth Warren characterized the decision as 'reckless,' and the author frames it as evidence that government leaders are influencing U.S. corporate governance rather than leaving boardroom decisions to independent directors—Nvidia's own announcement acknowledged receiving input from senior levels of the U.S. government before concluding Huang posed no national security risk. The article notes Nvidia's market value rose roughly $1 trillion in hours following his return, though it cautions that rising share prices do not address questions about Huang's conduct or his paramour's potential intelligence ties, nor explain why an independent board appears to have permitted a world leader to sway its decision while the investigation remains unfinished.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia CEO Amid Allegations and Government Involvement

items.summary:
Steven Greenhouse reported that Anthropic, the developer of Claude, raised $81 billion in its initial public offering—the largest IPO in history—valuing the company at $1.5 trillion. The financial windfall concentrated among a small elite: each of the seven co-founders received stakes worth roughly $20 billion, while an estimated 600 of Anthropic's more than 5,000 employees are projected to hold shares exceeding $100 million and another 2,800 with holdings above $10 million. Greenhouse framed this concentration as emblematic of broader U.S. wealth inequality, noting that many Americans resent the elite enrichment amid widespread distrust of AI's economic and existential risks, alongside grievances over datacenters that have raised electricity costs and disrupted communities.

The article presented a JP Morgan analysis estimating that corporations with AI ties account for 49% of the S&P 500's market value, warning that a 20% or 30% decline in those shares could severely damage millions of workers' and retirees' retirement accounts. This concern was supported by evidence that Anthropic's shares fell 9% on its IPO day as tech stocks declined more broadly, feeding fears of an AI stock bubble bursting into recession.

Greenhouse argued for a federal tax on IPOs or wealth tax to distribute some benefits publicly, while cautioning that the successful offering might embolden tech executives and President Trump—whose stated position opposes globalist regulation—to resist oversight. He acknowledged Anthropic's mitigating factors: its co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity stakes philanthropically, CEO Dario Amodei's advocacy for slowing AI development, the company's public-benefit-corporation mission, and his Nasdaq remarks acknowledging real risks. However, he noted that some experts like Dustin Moskovitz argue Anthropic is still advancing too quickly.
items.title: Anthropic's Record $81bn IPO Highlights Wealth Inequality and AI Concerns

items.summary: After Anthropic debuted on the stock market at a record $1.5 trillion valuation, its founders and employees are expected to channel newly available wealth into charitable giving, prompting nonprofits across global health, animal welfare, and poverty relief to prepare for an influx of donations. The company plans to dedicate 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, while its seven co-founders have committed to donating 80% of their equity — valued at $112 billion based on the IPO price. Stripe's Nan Ransohoff estimated in a May blog post that leading U.S. AI firms' valuations could add at least $37 billion annually in intended philanthropy, and Peter Singer characterized it as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to address extreme poverty. However, several caveats temper these projections: many Anthropic employees cannot sell or gift their shares until next spring, questions remain about the donors' charitable priorities given AI's rapid influence on worldviews, and sector volatility — including high borrowing costs, turmoil at Nvidia, and existential risk warnings — leaves skeptics doubtful about how much capital is actually available. Kumar Garg of Renaissance Philanthropy noted that deploying philanthropic capital remains difficult rather than automatic.
items.title: Anthropic's Record IPO Sparks Anticipation of a Wave of AI-Backed Philanthropy

items.summary:
The text reports on RoboTrack, a benchmark and training data suite designed to improve point tracking—the task of estimating where specific points appear across video frames—for real-world robotic manipulation. The central finding is that leading off-the-shelf trackers score significantly lower on the new benchmark than on existing robotics benchmarks, revealing weaknesses not captured by current evaluations.

RoboTrack-Bench contains 307 human-annotated videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2, and EgoVerse sources, totaling 2,522 human-verified point tracks. These clips feature robots and human hands manipulating objects across cluttered scenes in both first-person (ego) and third-person (exo) viewpoints, with a subset of 33 video pairs recorded simultaneously from two cameras for multi-view analysis. Annotators prioritized moving or occluded points over static background points, labeling each track as belonging to robot/human body, manipulated object, or static object.

Four trackers were evaluated—CoTracker3, BootsTAPNext, AllTracker, and CoWTracker—across RoboTrack-Bench plus four other benchmarks (RoboTAP for real-world tabletop manipulation, RGB-Stacking for simulated manipulation, DAVIS and Kinetics for general video). Performance was measured using Average Jaccard (AJ), where higher scores indicate better tracking accuracy and visibility prediction.

The key result is that every evaluated tracker scored lower on RoboTrack-Bench than on RoboTAP, the only other real-video robotics benchmark. Scores dropped by 3.0 to 6.6 AJ across models. The strongest off-the-shelf tracker, CoWTracker, fell from 70.5 AJ on RoboTAP to 63.9 AJ on RoboTrack-Bench. This consistent decline suggests existing benchmarks provide an incomplete picture of real-world manipulation tracking.

The text also examines why trackers struggle and how synthetic training data can help. Many trackers train on Kubric-generated videos showing objects tossed into scenes, which lack robot grasping examples. The authors extended MolmoSpaces (Ai2's simulation ecosystem) to generate dense point tracks from simulated robot manipulation trajectories—RoboTrack-15M contains 3,000 videos from 300 simulated homes with 5,000 tracks each, totaling 15 million tracks.

Adding RoboTrack-15M training improved performance: fine-tuning AllTracker (17 million parameters) into RoboTracker raised its AJ by 0.8 on RoboTrack-Bench (62.6 to 63.4), while fine-tuning CoWTracker (~1 billion parameters) into RoboTracker-Warp raised it by 2.1 AJ (63.9 to 66.0). Both models gained up to 1.2 AJ averaged across the three robotics benchmarks, with gains extending to other tracking benchmarks and on par performance on general video benchmarks.

RoboTracker-Warp achieved state-of-the-art performance on four of five evaluated benchmarks; DAVIS was the exception where BootsTAPNext and CoWTracker scored slightly higher. Breaking down improvements by source showed RoboTracker-Warp improved every dataset by roughly 1 to 3 AJ, including human footage from EgoVerse and Ego-Exo4D despite containing only robot arms.

The text notes several limitations: trackers still struggle with long occlusions, finding points when they reappear, and following small objects against busy backgrounds. Simulations focus on picking up everyday objects but don't yet capture precise movements like pipette handling. The authors acknowledge their AllTracker scores differ slightly from published ones due to a fixed scoring bug in released evaluation code.

Practical validation came through a wet-lab pipeline for guiding robot pipetting (transferring liquid between vials). Comparing three methods across 20 layouts—10 clear-view and 10 with partial occlusion—point tracking completed the full transfer in 17 of 20 trials versus 8 for object masks and 5 for optical flow. Point tracking succeeded in all 10 clear-view trials and 7 of 10 occluded ones, where mask-based methods succeeded only once.

The text presents two charts: one showing AJ scores across benchmarks by tracker (with robotics average over RoboTrack-Bench, RoboTAP, and RGB-Stacking), and another depicting success rates of pipetting trials with each method under clear-view versus occluded conditions. Both are supported by the article's value-and-unit pairs.
items.title: RoboTrack: Point Tracking for Real-World Robotic Manipulation

items.summary: IBM announced it would discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of roles in its consulting division, leaving affected employees with two options: relocate to a role abroad or exit the company. An IBM spokesperson attributed the decision to declining participation in U.S. high-skilled visa programs over several years as skill availability and client needs shifted. The company employs more than 150,000 people globally but does not disclose its geographical workforce split, making it difficult to determine how many workers are affected; on November 19 the career portal listed 1,278 open consulting roles outside the U.S.—including 1,125 in India, 23 in Singapore, and 18 in the U.K.—against only 89 within the U.S. Employees have three weeks to decide between relocation or a final work day of December 31 with three months of severance. Relocation is not guaranteed as an effective solution: experts note it may reduce access to decision-makers and networks, its credibility depends on tenure and compensation, and moving can require uprooting families while affecting spouses' employment and children's schooling. On the anonymous forum Blind—used by 14 million professionals—one employee reported that relocating to India could mean an approximately 80% pay cut. The move reflects a broader trend among U.S. tech firms under Donald Trump, with Amazon temporarily allowing stranded H-1B workers to work from India and Microsoft defending its international hiring after being suspended from the DOL's PERM green card program alongside Adobe and six other IT outsourcing firms including TCS and Infosys.
items.title: IBM Ends U.S. Visa Sponsorship for Most Consulting Roles, Offering Overseas Relocation

The reinstatement reverses a position taken during last week's earnings call, when the board said it would not bring him back after removing him on November 12 amid reports of numerous affairs with employees and a possible connection to a foreign intelligence official. Huang had confirmed an extramarital affair on November 8.

Support for reinstatement grew over the weekend from both President Donald Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who reversed earlier criticism—though Trump had been more supportive than Bessent initially. The article notes this move parallels Sam Altman's brief removal as OpenAI CEO in November 2023 and subsequent five-day reinatement.

Investigations into Nvidia remain ongoing despite the return: the SEC investigation opened after Huang's departure appears to continue, separate from national security concerns surrounding Alice Huang, whom Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair with. A board committee of independent directors retained independent counsel for its inquiry and reiterated that it would proceed to conclusion; Nvidia stated Huang supports the process and is committed to cooperating.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Ongoing Investigations

items.summary: Microsoft is testing a fix for a long-standing Windows issue that causes significant audio quality drops for users of Bluetooth headphones. The problem occurs when the operating system automatically switches from the high-quality A2DP stereo profile to the bandwidth-limited hands-free (microphone) profile whenever an app or game activates the headset's microphone, degrading sound during calls and gaming chat. According to Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines, installing preview builds released for the Beta and Experimental channels on Friday allows Insiders with newer Bluetooth headsets to maintain high-quality audio even after such profile switches. The fix supports all Bluetooth LE Audio devices capable of 48kHz playback—including headphones, earbuds, and speakers—and Microsoft directs users pairing an LE Audio device with a Super Wideband Stereo-capable PC to select the '2 channels, 16 bit, 48000Hz' output format from Settings when the microphone is active. The article notes this Bluetooth fix follows several other recent audio-related fixes: USB audio issues affecting devices after September security updates (USB Audio Class 1.0), a two-year-old block on Windows 24H2 upgrades for systems with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology drivers due to blue screen errors, and a January 2025 resolution of Code 10 playback errors tied to the KB5050094 preview update. The piece also mentions separate non-audio developments—testing of remote device-locking without wiping—and promotional content for Adaptive Security's AI phishing-fraud detection and email security scans, which are not part of the audio fix.
items.title: Microsoft Testing Fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth Audio Quality Drops

items.summary:
AlloyDB Omni, Google's PostgreSQL-compatible database that runs on-premises and in the cloud, now integrates with locally hosted large language models. According to Rob Yavitch, Senior Software Engineering Manager at AlloyDB Omni, this integration lets users build agentic experiences entirely within their own infrastructure while keeping data local. The system calls a local model server directly from SQL, so prompts, data, and responses stay inside the environment without crossing the public internet.

The architecture supports models like Gemma 4 from Google DeepMind and Qwen3.8, with Yavitch noting that the setup remains consistent regardless of which model is chosen. AlloyDB Omni retains its built-in AI features, including ScaNN indexing technology used in Google Search for storing vector embeddings at scale.

The integration enables use cases for air-gapped networks or environments with data locality requirements, allowing users to analyze local logs, summarize proprietary documents, and power localized chatbots while maintaining strict data governance. Yavitch lists three key benefits: keeping data on-premises by having the database and model in the same environment, reducing latency through local inference processing, and querying directly via SQL using built-in functions like ai.generate.

The article provides a step-by-step guide for testing this integration using Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), which Yavitch describes as offering a standardized but reproducible environment that can also be replicated on-premises. The setup requires users to have already configured a GKE cluster along with the kubectl and Helm tools, then proceeds through deploying the AlloyDB Omni Kubernetes Operator, creating the database while enabling googleMLExtension, deploying an AI model via Ollama (with Gemma 4 as the example), registering the model with SQL that includes output transform functions to strip chain-of-thought reasoning from responses, and finally testing queries using ai.generate. The article notes potential connection errors during provisioning may require waiting for database or model load completion.
items.title: AlloyDB Omni Adds Local LLM Integration for On-Premises AI

items.summary:
On Nov 23, OCBC announced the appointment of Ang Eng Siong—the current chief executive of OCBC China—as its new head of global corporate banking effective Jan 1, 2027. The move accompanies a reorganisation of the bank's wholesale banking business into three divisions aimed at sharpening focus across large corporations, multinational companies, financial institutions, public sector entities, and SMEs. Group CEO Tan Teck Long framed the restructuring as positioning OCBC to better serve customers amid what he described as a volatile environment.

Under the new structure, Ang will lead "GWB 1," which focuses on scaling the large corporate segment in core markets—Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Greater China—as well as overseas branches. Elaine Lam, who had headed global corporate banking since 2016, will take over "GWB 3" covering global institutional, investment, and transaction banking; GWB 3 is intended to strengthen capabilities in transaction banking, investment banking, structured finance, and the financial institutions group while expanding its mandate to include large alternative investment firms, asset managers, global institutions, and sponsors. Elaine Heng will continue leading "GWB 2," OCBC's current global commercial banking arm, with a focus on the SME segment.

Ang joined OCBC in July 2009 as a management associate, moved to China in 2015 for its corporate banking team, and was appointed CEO of OCBC China in 2023—a role he will retain until a successor is named. During his tenure there, the bank cited efforts around Greater China-Asean connectivity, cross-border wealth, differentiated customer propositions, and AI-driven digital transformation. Lam had grown the corporate banking franchise across specialised sectors since joining as a relationship manager in 2001.

The article notes that OCBC shares closed at $26.41 on Nov 23—down 0.5% or $0.13—before the announcement was made.
items.title: OCBC Appoints Ang Eng Siong as Global Corporate Banking Head Amid Wholesale Business Reorganisation

items.summary: In an essay published on Nov. 23, 2026 by Cristina Caffarra, the argument that Europe should accept its role as an AI 'middle power'—supplying factories while American hyperscalers and LLM labs build frontier models—is characterized as a defeatist trap rather than genuine leverage. The piece traces this narrative from earlier alarmism about denied access to frontier large language models (as dramatized in the 2018 provocation Europe 2031) toward its current industrial-AI permutation, which concedes that 'industrial AI is the watchword of the world's most uninspiring AI strategies' yet attempts to rehabilitate a version where America builds the models and Europe supplies manufacturing. Caffarra rejects this arrangement on three grounds: it relies on an innocent Ricardian division of labor (Europe has industrial assets, America has compute), that leverage guarantees Europeans a fair share of rent, and that terms can be written into enforceable contracts—asserting none of these assumptions holds because rents flow to the party with greater bargaining power, outside options determine that power, and long-term contracts are 'almost never enforceable.' The essay argues that once an industrial floor is deeply integrated with one LLM running on foreign infrastructure, Europe loses its outside options. It frames this as a repeat of what Caffarra calls Round 1 capitulation to American digital platforms—citing the example of two app stores and 2 million apps—to argue that Europe outsourced cloud, operating systems, app distribution, business software, search, advertising, communications, and data storage without recognizing it as a transfer of strategic power. The author contends that 'Middle Power leverage' is pushed by proxies for Silicon Valley, hyperscalers, LLM labs, Nvidia, think tanks with Silicon Valley money, and academics writing whitepapers on 'transformative AI,' all reinforcing the superiority myth of frontier models over open-weight alternatives (noting China's role). Caffarra concludes that Europe should instead pursue a deliberate reduction in dependence through building its own technological capacity, citing assets such as Mistral, multiple open-weight model sources, different architectures, and a budding cloud industry. The piece is an opinion essay advancing one author's critique; it offers no empirical data or independent verification of the claims about rent flows, contract enforceability, or platform dominance.
items.title: ‘Middle Power Leverage’ Framed as a Trap for Europe's Industrial AI

items.summary:
This November 23, 2026 article by Eliza McCullough, Tim Newman, and Aiha Nguyen argues that the AI economy increasingly depends on extracting worker data—particularly from physical labor—and calls for federal action to address it. The authors note that while most textual and visual training data is scraped online, companies are now turning to humans as a source of workplace data because robots require information about how people physically move and perform tasks.

The article's central evidence centers on the robotics sector: venture capital investment in robotics startups grew 185% in 2026 to roughly $10 billion per quarter, driven by claims that these systems could unlock a market worth upwards of $100 trillion (per an Nvidia executive). The authors attribute this optimism to an Nvidia executive's projection while noting a report from Anthropic contends robots are currently cost-effective substitutes for only 0.3% of job tasks—a figure the article says is echoed by additional reporting.

The extraction mechanism relies on "world models" trained on sensor, simulation, and egocentric data (first-person video captured from people performing tasks). Companies such as Scale AI, Micro1, Encord, Figure AI, Sanctuary AI, and Foundry Robotics collect this footage through platforms, facilities, or gig partnerships. Workers are recruited to film household tasks—sometimes for free services—and collection is becoming more granular via multi-camera headsets, brainwave headsets, and gloves. Participants span geographies and jobs, from waste management and garment workers in India to barbers, plumbers, HVAC experts, and DoorDash delivery workers in the US.

The authors attribute this dynamic to two factors: economic-political infrastructure protecting managerial prerogative (tracing it partly to Industrial Revolution-era labor frameworks) and gaps in labor protections. They note that while 24 states had passed data privacy laws as of October—and California's new workplace AI laws would ban emotion recognition and neural data collection—few cover workers specifically, and most laws focus on personal identifying information rather than the knowledge workers generate.

The article projects that near-term impact is roboticization of labor: Amazon already operates automated warehouses, Sanctuary AI describes building robots by gathering "an enormous amount of data from activities people would do if they were a robot," and Foundry Robotics raised $100 million to build factories designed around robots rather than existing production lines. The authors emphasize that the population at risk differs from generative-AI-exposed white-collar workers: those in construction, manufacturing, and logistics earn lower wages and are disproportionately Black and Latino.

The article's recommendations—attributed to scholars Salomé Viljoen (data value lies in aggregate patterns), Veena Dubal (a statutory ban on algorithmic wage discrimination), and California law—are for worker-centered privacy protections beyond notice-and-consent, prohibitions on business practices like emotion recognition and neural collection, and strengthening collective bargaining power through sectoral bargaining and empowered local enforcement. The authors frame these as necessary to shift technological development away from exploitation.

The article contains notable caveats: it attributes the $100 trillion figure to an Nvidia executive's belief rather than verified data; reports that worker pay often falls as competition increases, mirroring other platform sectors; and flags unresolved issues like unpaid labor, alleged wage theft, unexplained deactivation, health/safety concerns, and weakened federal institutions such as the NLRB. The authors also present their policy prescriptions as proposals requiring future action rather than established outcomes.
items.title: Robotics Is Coming for Workers' Data. It's Time for a National Response

items.summary: The article introduces RoboTrack, a benchmark and training data suite designed to evaluate point tracking in real-world robotic manipulation. The central finding is that leading off-the-shelf trackers perform significantly worse on realistic manipulation scenes than on existing robotics benchmarks.
items.title: RoboTrack: Point Tracking for Real-World Robotic Manipulation

items.summary: Tesla's FSD v15 represents the company's final opportunity to deliver unsupervised, Level 4 self-driving on its existing AI4 computer across millions of customer vehicles, according to Elon Musk. The software dedicates roughly half of one TRIP accelerator out of three on SoC B—about a billion-parameter diffusion model running off features from a 3B encoder—to Tesla Reality View, with Musk admitting the visualization's latency is elevated due to compute constraints and that this leaves little headroom for driving workloads. Engineer Dilreet Raju independently confirmed the hardware strain, describing his effort as co-designing the v15 vision encoder "to squeeze out the last few percents of MFU from AI4." The rollout also undermines Tesla's original 2019 redundancy design: cars shipped with two independent chips so one could take over if the other failed in an unsupervised system, but Musk indicated SoC B now runs both the decoder and Reality View rather than sitting idle as a mirror of SoC A. Tesla has not disclosed how much compute it reserves for failover or whether a single chip can safely bring a car to a stop alone—a gap highlighted by comparison with Waymo's publicly documented parallel systems, whose new custom chip exceeds 1,000 TOPS versus AI4's estimated 100–150 TOPS across both chips. The mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade is not a performance unlock but primarily an LPDDR5X memory swap; Musk cut its RAM from the originally announced 32GB down to 24GB citing cost and bandwidth constraints, while noting AI4's price doubled due to memory and storage hikes. Future hardware offers no escape hatch for current fleets: cars will remain on AI4 because both AI5 (described as roughly a 12x compute improvement) and AI6 are being redirected to Optimus robots and data centers, with Samsung's Texas fab not reaching AI5 volume until the second half of 2027. Tesla began v15 rollout Saturday claiming "25x better handling of safety critical cases" without any baseline, though early videos from testers emphasize UI features like Reality View rather than miles driven between interventions—the metric that matters for unsupervised driving.
items.title: Tesla FSD v15 Pushes AI4 to Compute Limits as Next-Gen Chips Diverted to Robots

items.summary: Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas extended his contract to lead the chip designer through 2033, confirming his continued leadership amid speculation that Nvidia could recruit him as its next chief executive. The speculation stems from Jensen Huang's resignation earlier in the month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. According to the Financial Times, Nvidia's board had approached Haas during its search for a successor; Colette Kress currently serves as interim CEO at Nvidia. Analysts cited Haas's long tenure with Nvidia—rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business before joining Arm in 2013—as making him a strong candidate, alongside his status as a high-profile semiconductor figure familiar with the company. In response to the speculation, US-listed shares of Arm rose nearly 9 per cent in premarket trading on November 23, riding a broader rebound in AI stocks after a selloff the prior week; Haas stated he had never been more confident about Arm's future and remained wholly committed to realizing its potential. Separately, Arm announced that Haas would assume the role of vice chairman of SoftBank Group effective December 1, building on his existing board membership and April takeover of SoftBank's international business operations.
items.title: Arm CEO Rene Haas Extends Contract Through 2033 Amid Nvidia Succession Speculation

items.summary: The NVIDIA board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and director with immediate effect, ending his interim absence. In his first public statement, Huang expressed gratitude for the board's decision and thanked interim leaders Harvey Jones (chair) and Colette Kress (interim CEO), who will retain their respective roles. The announcement coincided with a sharp stock rally: NVIDIA shares rose to $168.02 in premarket trading on Monday, up 33.85% from Friday's close of $125.53, adding roughly $1 trillion to market capitalization and potentially becoming the first company ever to add that amount in a single day if it closes at or above those levels. The rebound reversed heavy losses across AI-linked stocks during the prior week. Peer semiconductor companies also advanced—AMD and Broadcom each gained about 4%, Taiwan Semiconductor rose 6%, ASML gained 6%, Micron up roughly 5%, SK Hynix up about 9%—while AI infrastructure names CoreWeave and Nebius surged more than 25%. Anthropic's shares recovered approximately 5% after a Friday decline of 9%. Separately, the board confirmed that an independent investigation into reported foreign intelligence efforts targeting Huang would continue despite his reinstatement. The article presents these figures as premarket or intraday data from Yahoo Finance and does not provide closing prices to confirm whether NVIDIA actually achieved its projected $1 trillion daily market-cap gain.
items.title: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after board vote, triggering a more than 30% stock surge

items.summary: According to columnist Nils Pratley, Nvidia's board reversed its decision to remove co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang within roughly six days of the initial exit. The departure had originally been justified by Harvey Jones, newly installed as chair, citing disclosure of personal behaviour inconsistent with the company's code of conduct; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reinforced this stance, calling for an external hire amid scrutiny over export-control compliance. Pratley attributes the reversal to political pressure from senior levels of the US government: Trump stated he convinced the board to reinstate Huang as "a great patriot and national treasure," asserting that no reason existed to believe his return threatened national security. The investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort—and references to an alleged affair with Alice Huang, whom officials suspect of smuggling Nvidia chips into China—had not been completed at the time of reinstatement. Pratley links the reversal partly to falling AI share prices after the resignation and Trump's interest in preventing a burst of the AI valuation bubble, noting that roughly $1tn was instantly added back to Nvidia's valuation. He flags ongoing risks: Bessent had earlier pressed questions about Huang before his own U-turn, congressional scrutiny of export controls continues despite Nvidia forming a compliance committee, Rubio reportedly circulated an intelligence memo identifying Alice Huang as a Chinese spy, and Huang can no longer be trusted on export-control matters. Pratley concludes that the board reversed its largest decision under political pressure while forfeiting independence and without meaningful checks on Huang's power, arguing the directors should resign out of embarrassment.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reverses Jensen Huang's Ouster Under Political Pressure

items.summary:
In a 1,300-word blog post published Monday (November 23), Amazon's AWS CEO Matt Garman argued that reliable AI safety depends on engineering robust systems rather than relying on emergency controls such as kill switches. Framing his position around the analogy of vehicle brakes—where primary braking, steering, and navigation are engineered to work together while the emergency brake serves only as a last resort—Garman stated that trust in AI should be built by designing outcomes that remain controlled regardless of what runs inside a system.

The post was issued amid industry tensions: Anthropic's record-setting IPO this month contrasted with voter rejection of aggressive data-center buildouts and accelerated deployment, alongside researcher warnings earlier in the year about swarms of colluding agents breaching systems and evading safeguards. Garman positioned his engineering-focused approach as a response to what he called distracting "hype" around AI safety.

Concretely, Garman advocated for halting production of new models until they are safe even when competitors release them without adequate testing; limiting agent permissions so that at most an agent inherits the operating human's access and often has more constrained permissions; stress-testing model controls given software's tendency to act unexpectedly; and continuously monitoring models to prevent boundary violations. He concluded that leading AI organizations would be those investing in strong engineering discipline rather than simply deploying the best models.

The text presents these claims as Garman's stated positions without independent verification, and it does not provide supporting data or evidence beyond his assertions.
items.title: AWS CEO Matt Garman Argues Engineering, Not Kill Switches, Is the Path to AI Safety

items.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously voted Monday morning to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, president, and board director less than two weeks after he resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom U.S. officials believed had ties to Chinese intelligence. The decision followed meetings between the board and Huang, input from senior government levels, and statements that his return poses no national security risk; Nvidia's shares rose sharply on the announcement alongside broader market gains. President Trump endorsed the move as 'the correct and proper decision,' citing the need for Huang's leadership in AI policy and chip sales to China, though Nvidia's most advanced chips remain subject to export controls. The Justice Department is investigating Megaspeed over potential chip smuggling; Megaspeed stated Alice Huang left in 2025 while conducting an internal investigation. Nvidia maintains its ongoing inquiry into the foreign intelligence allegations against Huang, which he said he will cooperate with, and Trump directed continued review of the company's export control compliance as a board-formed committee oversees national security policies. The reinstatement reverses the board's November 17 position that it would not bring Huang back; Huang is expected to testify before congressional committees next week.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Amid National Security Review

items.summary: On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstituted co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, an action that added about $1 trillion to the chipmaker's market capitalization. The move followed intense pressure on the long-serving board after its stock fell 40% in a month, erasing roughly $2 trillion of value and prompting calls from investors, employees, and customers for Huang's return; the article attributes this decline partly to directors' failure to develop a credible succession plan. Nvidia's announcement—described as 465 words long—stated that input from senior levels of the U.S. government had reassured the board that Huang's return posed no national security risk, and Trump publicly endorsed rehiring Huang on Sunday, saying it would be best for both the company and the country; Semafor reported that Trump dialed into Nvidia's board meeting beforehand. The author frames this as a case of an 'imperial CEO' gaining unchecked power and views the episode as evidence that the Trump administration is willing to treat corporate America as an instrument of presidential power, signaling that decisions about who leads major companies may increasingly rest with the president rather than shareholders or their representatives.
items.title: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after a White House intervention, adding roughly $1 trillion to the company's market value

items.summary: NVIDIA shares rose more than 30% on Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as chief executive. In a research note dated November 23, Bernstein analysts Stacy A. Rasgon, Arpad von Nemes and Alrick Shaw reversed an earlier downgrade that had occurred just 11 days prior; the brokerage had cut NVIDIA's rating to Market Perform over concerns about Huang's leadership. The firm upgraded the stock back to Outperform while holding its $200 price target, citing attractive valuations and strong artificial intelligence fundamentals.
items.title: Bernstein Reaffirms NVIDIA Outperform Rating and $200 Target After Stock Surges on CEO Reinstatement

items.summary: The text reports that alphabetical ordering conventions may systematically advantage authors whose surnames begin with letters earlier in the alphabet, though it presents these claims as observations rather than established conclusions. In economics, where author listing has traditionally followed alphabetical order, faculty members at top departments with early-alphabet surnames are reported to be substantially more likely to achieve tenure, become Econometric Society fellows, and win Nobel prizes—examples cited include Arrow, Buchanan, and Coase. The text notes that no comparable effects appear in psychology, where the alphabetical norm is not followed. It also reports that the American Economic Association now permits coauthors to certify a randomized listing order using an ⓡ symbol (e.g., Ray ⓡ Robson), though alphabetical ordering remains the default practice. Separately citing Chris Dalla Riva's analysis of Grammy nominations from 2021 to 2025, when nominees were listed essentially alphabetically despite some messiness in details, the text reports that nominees with surnames beginning with A through E won at a rate higher than expected relative to their share on the Billboard charts. The framing throughout treats these patterns as suggestive evidence of an ordering bias rather than proven causation; the Grammy findings are explicitly flagged as messy and requiring fuller analysis elsewhere.
items.title: Alphabetical Ordering Bias in Academic Tenure and Award Nominations

items.summary: According to people familiar with the matter, President Trump dialed into Nvidia's board meeting to argue for CEO Jensen Huang's return hours before the company reinstated him on Monday. The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after receiving assurances from senior U.S. government levels that he posed no national security risk, despite allegations of an affair with a subordinate and accusations involving an alleged Chinese spy. White House communications director Steven Cheung characterized Trump as 'totally involved' in the decision. Nvidia's board met late Sunday evening; Harvey Jones, elevated to board chairman at Huang's Nov. 12 ouster, stated that the board believes Jensen is the right leader for NVIDIA and that his return serves stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. The anti-Jensen faction reportedly faced a setback when Arm CEO Rene Haas—considered a leading replacement candidate—signed a contract extending his employment until 2033. Huang returns to the company he founded in 1993 less than two weeks after stepping down under pressure, following outcry from some Silicon Valley figures and reports that a faction of directors had pushed for his return. Nvidia's stock rose nearly 30% in early Monday trading, its biggest gain in more than two decades. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, called the reinstatement 'reckless,' arguing it heightens urgency to pass bipartisan export control legislation and warning against NVIDIA lobbying efforts that could undermine national security protections.
items.title: Trump Called Nvidia's Board Hours Before Reinstating Jensen Huang

items.summary:
Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov. 23, just 11 days after he resigned over an admitted extramarital affair (Nov. 12). The reversal occurred during a broad tech selloff that pushed the Nasdaq negative for 2026 and fell about 10% in one week; Nvidia shares dropped roughly a third following Huang's departure, then rose nearly 30% after reinstatement—adding more than $1 trillion to market value. Analyst Dan Ives framed shareholders' risk as greater from losing the founder than retaining him. The board restored every role at once (Huang returned simultaneously as president and CEO), which the article notes makes it harder to distinguish vindication from necessity, since Huang again sits on the body that judged his conduct.

The decision followed a public pressure campaign: Nvidia employees urged restoration, 165,000 people signed a petition, and Elon Musk and Shopify's Tobias Lutke endorsed it. President Trump publicly argued national interest required Huang's leadership—calling him "a great patriot" while simultaneously directing the board to keep investigating export-control compliance—and reportedly told directors his administration provided security reassurance.

The article treats these as Nvidia's own account rather than independent confirmation, flagging key limitations: the reinstatement came before any wrongdoing was found or a national-security clearance issued; Trump—who also demanded Huang's return—was itself an assurance source, so no neutral review occurred. Oversight guardrails are partial and future-dependent: a National Security and Export Control Committee is still investigating whether Huang targeted foreign intelligence (with only Attorney General Todd Blanche named), the chief compliance officer post remains unfilled, interim CEO Colette Kress reverts to finance without changing who runs Nvidia, and both the SEC and Justice Department retain independent authority over legal exposure. Senators John Cornyn and Elizabeth Warren are cited as questioning whether the security assurance is sufficient.
items.title: Nvidia Reversed Jensen Huang's Exit in 11 Days Amid Market Selloff and Political Pressure

items.summary: National employment growth in the third quarter of 2026 accelerated slightly to 0.4% year over year, according to a report posted on November 23, 2026. At the state level, results varied more widely: 10 states lost jobs compared with one year earlier while the remaining 40 grew strongly, and the median state recorded job growth of roughly 0.4%. Growth also accelerated in 37 states between the second and third quarters. The report's color-coded maps were constructed by searching FRED for total nonfarm employees (for a state or an MSA such as St. Louis), viewing the map, editing it to use quarterly 'Percent Change from Year Ago' with an end-of-period aggregation method, and applying three user-defined color groups—red for states shedding jobs (values ≤ 0), light yellow for modest growth (below 0.7%), and dark green for strong growth.
items.title: State and Metro Employment: Third Quarter 2026

items.summary: Investing News Network ranked the largest publicly traded cybersecurity companies by market value, finding that Microsoft tops the list of ten with a $3.58 trillion valuation driven primarily by its cloud and Office businesses rather than security alone. The article's central thesis is that industry consolidation favors firms whose size derives from broader operations—cloud, software, or chips—with security treated as one product among many. Microsoft leads because it bundles security into Microsoft 365 and Copilot used by more than 1 billion people monthly; its Intelligent Cloud unit earned $34.7 billion in a quarter (up 30%), though shares fell 23.7% over six months amid heavy AI infrastructure spending. Amazon ranks second at $2.8 trillion, with AWS generating $17.8 billion of the company's $28.1 billion operating income; it is running a $42.4 billion free cash outflow while projecting more than 40% AWS revenue growth in both 2027 and 2028. Broadcom places third at $1.81 trillion as a chipmaker that acquired security brands (Carbon Black, Symantec) rather than building them; its semiconductor unit earned $20.8 billion versus $8.75 billion for software, with AI revenue targeting of $230 billion by fiscal 2028. Cisco ranks fourth at $439.9 billion after its ~$28 billion Splunk acquisition, which CEO Chuck Robbins pitched as a growth strategy though integration risks remain unproven. Palo Alto Networks ($304.92 billion) is the largest pure-play specialist, with revenue up 39% and an agreed $4.5 billion stock deal for Applied Compute expected to add over $1 billion in recurring revenue by fiscal 2029 (pending a third-quarter 2027 close). IBM ranks sixth at $219.21 billion on breadth rather than strength, committing $5 billion with Red Hat's engineers to Project Lightwell; CrowdStrike ($216.81 billion) earned nearly as much value from security alone despite reporting just $24.9 million in quarterly profit and agreed an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler at ~$43.9 billion (pending approval). Fortinet ranks eighth at $115.93 billion, Cloudflare ninth at $107.31 billion—though its claims that 45% of Fortune 500 companies use it and over 20% of the internet runs through it are unconfirmed—and Zscaler is smallest at $30.03 billion before being absorbed by CrowdStrike, illustrating consolidation where the year's winner buys the laggard.
items.title: Microsoft Leads the 10 Largest Cybersecurity Companies at US$3.58 Trillion

items.summary:
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York post by Jeffrey B. Dawson, Matthew Higgins, and Chanwoo Kim argues that the United States is approaching demographic headwinds already experienced across advanced economies (AEs), where near-zero working-age population growth—driven by declining net immigration—is threatening to shrink labor supply.

Since 2014, working-age populations have contracted in seven of the sixteen largest AEs shown, with particularly sharp declines in Japan (-7%), Italy, Poland, and Taiwan. The median AE also saw negative growth, while several countries posted gains exceeding 5%. U.S. growth was positive at roughly 3%, placing it below most peers.

Prime-age (25-54) populations fared worse than overall working-age figures in many economies: Japan (-6%), Germany (~-2% with over -8% prime-age decline), Italy, and Spain all contracted sharply. The gap between these columns—especially visible in Spain—is attributed to population aging as cohorts move into the 55-64 group.

Labor force growth defied demographic gravity across AEs: Japan added ~6% labor force on a -7% working-age drop; Germany grew nearly 6% despite its decline. In the broader sample of thirty-six AEs, only Greece and Latvia saw small declines.

This divergence is explained by rising participation rates. The median AE gained about 4 percentage points (ppt) in overall participation since 2014, with women contributing over 5 ppt at the median. "Young old" (65-74) gains were even larger—Japan led at roughly 12½ ppt, Korea and the Netherlands close behind.

However, these buffers are finite: matching current leaders' participation rates to Italy's would be equivalent to a ~26% increase in its working-age population; for the U.S., raising engagement to about 85% could add roughly 13%. The authors caution that this upside may not materialize and note Korea as an early warning—its Bank of Korea projects peaking around 2028 before declining, with limited immigration offering little offset.

Immigration emerged as the dominant driver: every AE except Israel saw fertility fall below replacement by the mid-1970s. Every country whose working-age population rose from 2014 to 2025 recorded substantial net immigration (several percentage points of initial stock). Relative to its size, the U.S. did not stand out; the UK, Sweden, and Switzerland benefited more.

The authors conclude that future labor supply will depend critically on policy choices around immigration and participation—both finite or uncertain margins.
items.title: Foreign Demographic Trends as a Preview of U.S. Labor Supply Pressures

items.summary:
President Trump told CNBC that he spoke 'directly and indirectly' with Nvidia's board about reinstating CEO Jensen Huang, saying the administration gave assurances on national security risks after the board requested them. He also said he personally spoke with Huang before his reinstatement was announced, arguing it would be a greater threat to lose Huang's expertise than to bring him back.

The reinstatement follows reports that Alice Huang, Jensen's wife, contacted an official in China's Ministry of State Security for over a year during their affair. Trump claimed the government conducted 'a very thorough investigation' and concluded Huang did nothing wrong but had poor judgment on unrelated matters.

The commission rejected these positions on three grounds: respondents failed to submit an expert technician report proving the faults were not manufacturing defects; there was no admission by the consumer that he mishandled the device; and respondents provided no evidence linking the damage to his negligence. Virginia's attorney general stated that the companies failed to prevent creation and distribution of such images despite publicly assuring consumers that safeguards were in place.

The allegations are unproven; Jones emphasized they have not been established by a court, and both actions seek civil relief rather than criminal prosecution. The cases add to litigation SpaceX had already disclosed to investors: its September 30 quarterly filing with the SEC reported multiple lawsuits alleging Grok's image-generation features enabled nonconsensual explicit images or sexualized depictions of women and children.

That disclosure preceded Monday's announcement, though it did not respond to the newly announced cases. The same SEC filing noted that Virginia had sent a notice on October 19 warning of possible litigation over representations about Grok's capabilities and limitations of its safeguards—also preceding the lawsuits. Both attorneys general framed their allegations around both creation of harmful images and assurances made to users, with Virginia noting exposure can cause distress while circulation of manipulated images causes continuing harm to targeted individuals.
items.title: Virginia and Oregon Sue Elon Musk Companies Over Alleged Grok AI Nonconsensual Image Generation

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India proposed on Monday allowing bank customers to nominate a trusted adult who must authenticate electronic fund transfers exceeding a customer-defined threshold within one hour, or the transaction will be cancelled. Initially introduced in April as an optional safeguard for senior citizens aged 70 and above, the facility has been extended voluntarily to all bank customers under draft guidelines. The RBI dropped its earlier proposal for a mandatory one-hour cooling period on large-value digital transactions, instead favoring customer-controlled safeguards that do not apply to UPI transfers, merchant payments, or recurring payment mandates. Banks must also provide an emergency 'Stop Switch' facility enabling instant blocking of outward debits, and customers can set per-transaction limits and disable electronic transfers during specified periods. The draft holds banks liable for losses arising from negligence—including failure to implement multi-factor authentication, send transaction alerts, or prevent internal security breaches—though these provisions are not yet in force; the trusted person mechanism, Stop Switch facility, and other controls are scheduled to become mandatory on July 1, 2027, while bank-negligence definitions take effect January 1, 2027, both subject to public feedback.
items.title: RBI Proposes 'Trusted Person' Approval for Online Fund Transfers

items.summary: The Indian government's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), through its National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, issued an advisory cautioning users against leaving active WhatsApp Web sessions logged in on shared or public computers. According to the agency, a persistent session enables unauthorised individuals to read private messages and contact lists, view group conversations, and send messages while impersonating the account holder—risks that could expose users to phishing attacks, financial fraud, and other scams. The advisory clarifies that simply closing a browser window or tab does not terminate an authenticated WhatsApp Web session; users must manually select logout instead. It recommends avoiding public systems such as cyber cafes, kiosks, hotel business centres, and borrowed devices, using Incognito or Private Browsing mode when access is unavoidable while still logging out before closing the browser, refraining from exchanging government, financial, organisational, or confidential information over WhatsApp Web on computers, monitoring for unexplained activity like unexpected outgoing messages, and keeping operating systems, browsers, and security software updated. Users who suspect account compromise are advised to review linked devices in WhatsApp settings and log out of unfamiliar sessions, with the option to report fraud through the national cybercrime helpline at 1930 or the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. The text does not provide independent verification of these claims beyond the I4C advisory itself.
items.title: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre Warns Against Leaving WhatsApp Web Logged In on Shared Computers

items.summary: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) of India's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) issued an advisory dated November 18 warning that authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions could be exploited to gain unauthorised access to users' accounts. According to the unit, such access would allow malicious actors to read messages, impersonate account holders, and reach contacts and group conversations for purposes including fraud, phishing, social engineering, and other malicious activities. The advisory specifically cautioned against keeping authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions permanently logged in—particularly on office or shared computers—and urged users to manually log out after every session rather than simply closing a browser window or tab, which the unit clarified does not constitute logging out. For unavoidable use of WhatsApp Web, it recommended Incognito or Private Browsing mode and access only from trusted computers, while advising against login attempts via cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed devices, or other untrusted systems. In official and sensitive environments, organisations were advised to avoid using WhatsApp Web on office computers entirely, with private browsing framed as an additional precaution rather than a substitute for this guidance. The advisory also directed users to remain alert to unusual account activity—such as unexpected messages sent from their accounts—and to keep operating systems, browsers, and security software updated while avoiding suspicious downloads, unknown files, cracked software, and untrusted sources. I4C was established by the Union home ministry to serve as a coordinated framework for law enforcement agencies addressing cybercrime nationally; however, these recommendations reflect an advisory posture rather than confirmed vulnerabilities or incidents tied to WhatsApp Web specifically.
items.title: Indian Government Warns Against Using WhatsApp Web for Official Work Amid Account Access Risks

items.summary: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of India's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) issued an advisory warning that keeping a WhatsApp Web session active on office PCs, laptops, or shared systems can expose private chats and enable online fraud. According to the agency, cybercriminals could exploit these open sessions to access personal messages, contacts, and group conversations, and unauthorised users might send messages impersonating account holders to target friends, family, and colleagues through phishing and financial scams. The advisory specifically flagged that closing a browser tab or window does not necessarily log out of WhatsApp Web; an authenticated session may persist on the same device, allowing someone with access to reopen it and view conversations. To mitigate these risks, the I4C recommended manually logging out after every session—especially on office computers, shared devices, cyber cafés, public kiosks, hotel business centres, or borrowed machines—and using incognito or private browsing mode when accessing an unfamiliar computer is unavoidable. It also advised against sharing government-related, financial, organisational, or other confidential information through WhatsApp Web sessions and urged users to watch for unexpected messages from their account or unusual replies from contacts. The agency further recommended keeping devices, browsers, operating systems, and security software updated; avoiding suspicious downloads, unknown files, and cracked software; and remaining alert to unauthorised account activity that could expose private information and put contacts at risk of fraud.
items.title: India's I4C Warns That Leaving WhatsApp Web Logged In on Shared Computers Exposes Chats to Hacking and Fraud
